title: Assessment 3: After the Full SHINE Project

administration.sourceTimingNote: NOTE:  Administer after students complete the independent study using real-world data.

instructions: INSTRUCTIONS:  This assessment is a required activity for all students participating in the SHINE Project and it is also being used for research purposes by the SHINE project leadership team (Drs. Esther Isabelle Wilder, Gregory Broberg, Eduardo Vianna, and Toni Watt).  If you wish to be a participant in the SHINE Research Program, you must complete the Institutional Research Board (IRB) consent form prior to completing this assessment.  Please complete this assessment on your own and in one sitting.  Please try your best on every item.

content.text: Questions 1-3 use the table below. Eight students reported their entry pathway and the number of data sources they reviewed.

Questions 5-7 concern whether students who worked with a peer mentor were more likely to submit a revised analysis. Twenty students participated: 8 worked with a mentor and 12 did not. Five mentored students and 9 students without a mentor submitted a revision.

sections.title: Attitudinal Questions
instructions: For each statement, select the response that best represents how you feel at this point. Use the same scale for every statement.

questions.prompt: I am comfortable entering data into a spreadsheet such as Excel or Google Sheets.
I feel confident using spreadsheet software to carry out simple data analysis.
I am comfortable calculating percentages.
I feel confident interpreting percentages.
I am comfortable working with rates and ratios.
I feel confident reading bivariate tables that compare two variables.
I feel confident reading and interpreting graphs.
I feel confident distinguishing between row percentages and column percentages in a table.
I feel confident explaining the results of quantitative analysis in words.
I am interested in learning more about quantitative data analysis.
It is fun to work with spreadsheet software.
I find working with data and numbers enjoyable.
I enjoy quantitative problems that challenge me.
Courses that require working with data and numbers are stressful for me.
Data analysis is a difficult skill.
Data analysis is boring.
I try to avoid taking math and quantitative courses.
I plan to take the bare minimum number of math or statistics courses I need to take in college.
Data analysis is helpful for understanding content in non-math classes.
Data analysis is an important skill to learn in college.
The best way to learn data analysis is through class projects.
Learning to analyze data is worth the effort.
Data analysis skills will be useful for my future education or career.
Being good at data analysis will help me make decisions about issues that matter to me or my community.
All people have the ability to improve their quantitative skills.
I think of myself as a math/quantitative person.

sections.title: Experience with the Independent Study
instructions: Note:  Use the same 1-7 agreement scale shown in Part 1.

questions.prompt: The topic of my independent study was meaningful to me.
I had a meaningful role in developing or refining the research question.
Working with real-world data made the project more interesting.
The project helped me identify independent and dependent variables.
The project strengthened my ability to calculate and interpret rates, ratios, or percentages.
Making tables helped me recognize patterns in the data.
Making graphs helped me communicate the results.
The project strengthened my ability to interpret bivariate relationships.
My mentor was available when I needed guidance.
The feedback I received from my mentor improved my project.
I felt comfortable asking my mentor questions.
My mentor encouraged me to make my own research decisions.
Overall, working with my mentor was a positive experience.
The project strengthened my identity as a STEM researcher.
The project increased my interest in taking additional STEM or data-focused courses.
The project increased my interest in participating in research again.
The project influenced my thinking about my future educational goals.
The project influenced my thinking about possible careers.
I would be interested in completing another project that uses real-world data.
I would recommend completing an independent research project like this to other students.
Briefly state your research question or project topic, your most important finding, and the quantitative evidence that best supports it.
What was the most valuable or interesting part of completing your own research project?
Describe your experience working with your mentor. What did your mentor do that was most helpful?
Did this experience affect the way you think about yourself as a STEM researcher? Please explain.
Did this experience affect your future educational or career aspirations? If so, how?
How did the gamification platform prepare you for the independent study, if at all?

sections.title: Cognitive Questions
instructions: Select the best answer for each question. A calculator and spreadsheet software may be used for this portion of the assessment, but please do not use any artificial intelligence to look up the answers.  We use this assessment to evaluate the effectiveness of our program and to design instructional practices that best serve students, but not to evaluate individual students.  Your performance on the assessment does not affect your standing in the SHINE program.
